sentences.text: Scientists identified nine unique physical traits that distinguish this dinosaur from all others.
The skull measured forty-three centimeters in length.
Its eye socket was exceptionally large, taking up forty percent of the total skull length.
A bone called the jugal displayed an unusual L-shape with a very long front branch and a nearly missing rear branch.
A cable-like structure with a constant diameter of three millimeters ran parallel to the ribs on the outside of the neck.
This feature started directly behind the skull and extended along several vertebrae for several meters.
The neck itself possessed an oval cross-section and a rough, striated surface texture.
Moderately elongated teeth showed sharply angled wear facets and a unique orientation.
Researchers estimated the animal reached a length of twelve meters and weighed ten tonnes.
The eye socket was so large it equaled forty percent of the skull's total length.
A cable-like structure with a constant diameter of three millimeters ran along the neck for several meters.
The teeth had a unique orientation that suggests a special, currently unexplained method of cropping vegetation.
A sauropod skull was discovered in 1997 by Rubén D.F. Martínez at the Estancia Laguna Palacios in Chubut province.
The species Sarmientosaurus musacchioi was named and described in 2016 by a team including Rubén D.F. Martínez and Lawrence M. Witmer.
The genus name Sarmientosaurus refers to the town of Sarmiento.
The species name honors the late Eduardo Musacchio, an educator at the Universidad Nacional de la Patagonia San Juan Bosco.
The holotype specimen represents an elderly individual.
Researchers assumed the structure was an ossified tendon internal to a neck muscle, rather than a continuation of a neck rib.
The internal structure of the tendon indicates that it ossified rapidly at a young age.
Based on ear and neck tendon evidence, Sarmientosaurus likely held its head and neck down low, similar to the character Eeyore.
This low head posture implies Sarmientosaurus may have fed on lower-lying plants compared to other sauropods.
Sarmientosaurus had very large eye sockets, suggesting it may have had better vision than other titanosaurs.
Sarmientosaurus is classified within the unranked family Lithostrotia.
Martínez and colleagues placed Sarmientosaurus in a basal position within the clade Lithostrotia, above Malawisaurus on the evolutionary tree.
Sarmientosaurus lived in what is now Argentina during the Upper Cretaceous Period, approximately 95 million years ago.
Remains were found in Argentina in strata dating from the Cenomanian to Turonian stages of the Upper Cretaceous Period.
Sarmientosaurus lived between 100.5 and 89.8 million years ago.
In 2021, Stephen Poropat and colleagues reclassified Sarmientosaurus as part of the clade Diamantinasauria, along with Savannasaurus and Diamantinasaurus.
The correlation between the inner ear structure and head posture has been questioned in previous studies.
